unit.title: Introduction to Electrical Energy and DC Circuits

title: Dependent sources and passive circuit elements — R, L and C
summary: Dependent/controlled sources (VCCS, CCCS, CCVS, VCVS); resistance, inductance and capacitance definitions, units, voltage-current relations, DC behaviour and energy relations.
transcription_policy: Notebook order and meaning are preserved; grammar, punctuation and awkward English are lightly cleaned for study. Crossed-out corrections are normalized to the final readable wording, and no new theory is added unless explicitly marked as a short clarification.

mapped_topics.label: Electrical energy sources: voltage, current, independent and dependent sources
Circuit elements: resistance, inductance and capacitance

blocks.text: If the voltage or current of a source depends on another voltage or current elsewhere in the network, it is called a dependent or controlled source.
Notation used in the summary table: \(V_c\) and \(I_c\) are the controlling voltage and current; \(V\) and \(I\) are the dependent-source output.

blocks.caption: Four dependent sources — class notation and equation terms

rows.alt: VCCS dependent-current-source symbol: diamond with upward arrow.
CCCS dependent-current-source symbol: diamond with upward arrow.
CCVS dependent-voltage-source symbol: diamond with plus above minus.
VCVS dependent-voltage-source symbol: diamond with plus above minus.

items.title: Understanding the four dependent sources
paragraphs: Read each name as “what controls it” followed by “what the source produces”. For example, Voltage-Controlled Current Source means a voltage elsewhere in the circuit controls the current produced by this dependent source.
The controlling quantity is not the output of the diamond source itself. It is a voltage or current elsewhere in the network that the dependent source responds to.
For a voltage-output dependent source (VCVS or CCVS), the diamond symbol has voltage polarity \(+/-\). For a current-output dependent source (VCCS or CCCS), the diamond contains a current arrow.

The constant tells how strongly the output responds to the control quantity. \(A_v\) and \(A_i\) are dimensionless gains; \(G_m\) converts control voltage into output current; \(R_m\) converts control current into output voltage.

items.title: What each term in the equations means
paragraphs: The symbols in the four relations separate the controlling quantity from the output of the dependent source. The subscript \(c\) means “controlling”.
The gain or transfer constant tells how much output is produced for a given control quantity. Its units depend on whether the input and output are voltages or currents.
bullets: \(V_c\) — controlling voltage elsewhere in the circuit.
\(I_c\) — controlling current elsewhere in the circuit.
\(V\) — output voltage produced by the dependent voltage source.
\(I\) — output current produced by the dependent current source.
\(G_m\) — transconductance: output current per unit controlling voltage. Unit: A/V = siemens (S), also called mho.
\(A_i\) — current gain: output current divided by controlling current. It has no units.
\(R_m\) — transresistance: output voltage per unit controlling current. Unit: V/A = \(\Omega\).
\(A_v\) — voltage gain: output voltage divided by controlling voltage. It has no units.
The subscript \(m\) in \(G_m\) and \(R_m\) is part of the parameter symbol here; it is not the metric prefix “milli”.

blocks.text: Resistance is the property of a circuit element that opposes the flow of current. It is represented by \(R\).

blocks.alt: Notebook-style resistor symbol: a short horizontal lead, zig-zag resistor element and short horizontal lead.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Resistor symbol

blocks.text: Energy is consumed by a resistor; it cannot store or deliver energy.
For constant power, \(W=Pt\); for constant voltage and current, \(W=VIt\).
Inductance is the property of a circuit element that opposes a change in current. It is represented by \(L\).

blocks.alt: Notebook-style inductor symbol: a short horizontal lead, a compact series of coil loops and a short horizontal lead.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Inductor symbol

blocks.text: The inductance of a coil is defined as the ratio of flux linkage to the current flowing through the coil.
\(\phi\) = flux in weber; \(N\) = number of turns; \(i\) = current in amperes.
If the current through an ideal inductor is constant, \(di/dt=0\), so it acts as a short circuit to DC.
An ideal inductor stores energy when the current through it changes. It does not consume energy; it stores energy.

blocks.alt: Notebook-style capacitor symbol with two straight parallel plates, horizontal leads, plus above the left plate and minus above the right plate.
blocks.caption: Class-note redraw · Capacitor symbol

blocks.text: Any two conducting surfaces separated by an insulating dielectric exhibit capacitance. The conducting surfaces are called electrodes, and the insulating substance is called the dielectric.
If the voltage across an ideal capacitor is constant, \(dv/dt=0\), so \(i=0\); the capacitor acts as an open circuit to DC.
A capacitor stores energy when the voltage across it changes. A pure capacitor does not consume energy; it stores energy.
